{{Quote|<s></s>''Home One'', this is Gold Leader.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], during the Battle of Endor|<ref name="RotJ" />}}
'''''Home One''''', also known as the '''Headquarters Frigate''', was an [[MC80 Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic's]] [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]], famous for its role at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and as one of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagships]].<ref name="RotJ" /> It was the namesake of the [[MC80A Home One Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|''Home One'' type subclass]]<ref name="SOTG07" /> and was noted as being the largest and most advanced of the Rebel Star Cruisers.<ref name="RotJn">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref><ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:Home_One_briefing_room.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The briefing room on ''Home One''.]]
''Home One'' belonged to the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] line of warships, and like most Mon Cal ships, it had a long cylindrical [[Hull/Legends|hull]]. Blue-gray in [[Color/Legends|color]], it had a tapered nose, and a bulbous stern, and it lacked the flared wings seen on the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 ''Liberty'' type]].<ref name="RotJ" />

In her original form, the ''Home One'' was an unarmed civilian vessel, designed for deep-space exploration, and her hull was strewn with a number of large observation [[Viewport/Legends|viewports]] that would have been vulnerable in a military role. However, it is possible that, viewport bubbles notwithstanding, she was protected from the outset by the heavy hull plating and triple-redundant [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] that she would later carry in Rebel Alliance service.<ref name="FF" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the ''Home One'' was rebuilt to serve as a [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]], [[Carrier/Legends|carrier]] and [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]].<ref name="RAS" /> Her vast viewports were plated over, and she was outfitted with a heavy offensive armament.<ref name="SOTG07" />

The hull contained twenty [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]], two of which were capable of handling larger vessels,<ref name="A Guide 2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> these presumably being the large bay on the starboard side of the hull,<ref name="RotJ" /> and the main hangar on the ship's underbelly.<ref name="FF" /> Two smaller bays were visible on the port side of the hull, approximately opposite the large starboard bay.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi]]'' This is a production photo of the special-effects model built for ''Return of the Jedi'', but the port-side bays are not clearly visible on-screen.</ref> The secret squadron [[Stealth Squadron|Gray Flight]] utilized a hangar with an aperture located in the "ceiling" of the room.<ref name="DHSW7">[[Star Wars (2013) 7|''Star Wars'' (2013) 7]]</ref> The interior corridors, [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridges]] and bulkheads of the ''Home One'' were pristine white.<ref name="RotJ" />

[[File:Home_One-TCG_Core_Set.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Home One'' in action.]]
The ''Home One'' was modified by Calamari [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] to be capable of splitting apart in three sections. The topmost section containing the main bridge and a forward section above the bow could separate from the main superstructure and function as additional warships or escape vehicles.<ref name="SW:CV" />

The ship was powered by four [[M8.0-StarDrive engine]]s and six [[M4.5-StarDrive maneuvering engine/Legends|M4.5-StarDrive maneuvering engines]], a drive system also used on the ''Liberty'' type,<ref name="The Rebel Alliance" /> although the [[Engine/Legends|thrusters]] of the two designs were arranged in different configurations: where the ''Home One'' had four large and six small nozzles, the ''Liberty'' had nine of varying sizes.<ref name="RotJ" />

''Home One'' had a standard crew of 5,402, in addition to 78 [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]]. It could carry 1,200 troops and 20,000 [[Metric ton/Legends|metric tons]] of cargo<ref name="SOTG07" /> The minimum operating crew for the vessel was 1,230. As with all early Mon Calamari cruisers, most ship bridge controls could not be modified for use by [[Human/Legends|Human]] hands, so the command crews were almost exclusively Mon Calamari,<ref name="FF" /> but the rest of the crew were a mix of all Rebel species: for example, [[Isplourrdacartha Estillo|Plourr Ilo]] served as a technician during the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Rogue Handbook">[[Star Wars Handbook 1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|''Star Wars Handbook'' 1: ''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

==History==
As with most Alliance-era Mon Calamari warships, the ''Home One'' began as a civilian vessel built at the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] of [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]]. She was designed as an unarmed exploration vessel, used to investigate deep space and to make contact with alien species.<ref name="FF" />

[[File:Homeonefires.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Home One'' fires its forward batteries.]]

When the Mon Calamari began to support the Alliance in earnest, the ship was selected for conversion into a warship, and became the flagship of the recently freed [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]]. ''Home One'' became particularly important after the Alliance's defeat at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] deprived [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] of a planetary headquarters, and she became the mobile base of operations of the Rebel leadership. As the flagship of Admiral Ackbar, [[Supreme Allied Commanders|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]], the vessel was considered one of the most important assets to the Rebellion.<ref name="MCSCitDB">{{DB|starship|moncalamaristarcruiser|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser}}</ref>

''Home One'' was one of the largest ships in the Alliance fleet at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and Ackbar commanded the Alliance fleet from its bridge.<ref name="RotJn" /> [[X2]] helped Ackbar defend the ship's [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]] from attacking [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="ES PSP">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]''</ref> The vessel went on to serve as Ackbar's flagship for the next five [[Standard year/Legends|years]], serving as the home base of the famed [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] unit [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] and participating in numerous key battles, including the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Seizure of Coruscant]],<ref name="XW:WG" /> the [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Battle of Bilbringi]],<ref name="TLC">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> and the [[Battle of Ciutric]].<ref name="XW:IR">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref>

Ackbar's flagship was constantly in use, due to the Supreme Commander's tendency to command important engagements personally. As a result, the vessel needed to be maintained at a constant state of readiness, which was achieved by repair yards in orbit over [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref>

[[File:HomeOne_command_deck.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Admiral Ackbar and one of his officers during the Battle of Endor.]]

Over the years, however, more advanced Mon Calamari starships were developed, such as the [[MC80B Star Cruiser|MC80B]] and [[MC90 Star Cruiser|MC90]], and by [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], Ackbar was commanding the fleet from a new MC90 Star Cruiser, the [[Defiance (MC90 Star Cruiser)|''Defiance'']].<ref name="Dark Empire">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''.</ref> But the ''Home One'' continued to be deployed in front-line roles. She served as the command ship in the hunt for [[Leonia Tavira]]'s [[Invids|Invid]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], leading a taskforce that included [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] and two [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyers]],<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> and Ackbar continued to use the venerable Star Cruiser as [[Gender/Legends|his]] personal flagship throughout his tenure as [[Supreme Commander (Alliance)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], so she did not leave service until [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]] at the earliest.<ref name="FF" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Falcon-hangar.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Matte painting of the hangar deck on board ''Home One''.]]
Canon is inconsistent about the weapons array aboard ''Home One''. The best-known (and apparently most frequently stated) armament consists of 29 turbolasers and 36 ion cannons, arguably a very light armament for a vessel of this cruiser's size and importance. However, the earliest known source to give the ship's armament, the 1984 [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe|first edition of ''A Guide to the Star Wars Universe'']], describes her as carrying 29 batteries of five turbolaser cannon each, for a more impressive total of 145 turbolasers and 36 ion cannons. Adding to the confusion, the ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'' gives ''Home One'' instead an armament of 48 turbolasers and 20 ion cannons, which had previously been given as the armament of a standard [[MC80 Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]]. ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 12]]'' cites the two contrasting armaments on consecutive pages. A more recent official source, [[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'']], gives the ''Home One'' and its subclass 36 turbolasers, 36 heavy ion cannons and six tractor beam projectors.

In the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization of ''Return of the Jedi'']] and a number of other early sources, the name ''Headquarters Frigate'' was italicized as if it were the ship's name, and "Home One" (or "Home-one") was not, as if it were merely a [[Callsign/Legends|Call sign]] for the ship, comparable to "[[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]]."

Some fans have wondered how a ship can be called both a "cruiser" and a "frigate," but a possible real-world parallel is found in the United States Navy, where the term "frigate" was used for all but one of the large surface-combat warships built between [[1950s|1950]] and [[1975]], the majority of which were reclassified as "cruisers" in 1975.

[[File:HomeOneScaling-EaW.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''Home One'' scaled against two ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers, from ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''.]]

The game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' scales ''Home One'' at approximately 3,200 meters. The game shows the ''Venator'', ''Victory'', ''Imperial'', and ''Liberty'' classes in nearly perfect relative scale against each other. "Character" vessels are sometimes larger than their counterparts, which suggests that ''Home One'' may not be to scale, though the scaling is consistent with its size in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="EaW" />

[[The LEGO Group]] made a set of the ''Home One'' called "Home One Mon Calamari Star Cruiser" released in [[August]] [[2009]]. The set focused on the briefing room and a hanger bay rather than the whole ship.

In the ''Rogue Squadron'' games, the ''Home One''{{'s}} docking bay often acted as the main area to select spacecraft for a mission, with the exception of missions relating to [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]] or [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], for which the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple's]] docking bay and the [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] docking bays, respectively, acted as that area instead.
